activities.anchor: investigation is not intensified news work but a different structure
activities.caption: slide between the daily story and the assembled case
activities.name: invStructureCompare

config.prompt: Same facts, different structure — slide between the daily news story and the investigation.

before.label: Daily news story
before.text: A claim arrives; it is verified to a deadline and published. The unit of work is the story, and speed is part of the value.

after.label: Investigation
after.text: A hypothesis is tested against records, witnesses and numbers for months. The unit of work is a case, and the counter-case is written before publication.

config.why: The lesson's distinction: intensity is not the difference — structure is. The daily story verifies a claim; the investigation assembles a case.

activities.anchor: If your story lives only in what a whistleblower says and dies without the records, it is not ready.
activities.caption: bet first — the spine of a landmark investigation
activities.name: invSpinePredict

config.q: What is the spine of nearly every landmark investigation?
choices: Public documents any citizen could request
config.why: Sources add explanation and direction; the documents carry the case. If it dies without the records, it is not ready.

activities.anchor: misquoted subjects are the cheapest way to lose a lawsuit and a story.
activities.caption: fill the blanks — the sourcing floor
activities.name: invSourceCloze

config.text: The two-source rule is the %%0%%, not the ceiling: material allegations get %%1%% corroboration where documents exist, and the notebook records the exact question behind each quote.
config.hint: One word names the minimum standard; the other names the kind of corroboration the lesson prefers.

activities.anchor: Skilled interviewers plan all three before booking a room
activities.caption: pair each evidence-interview mode with its logic
activities.name: invInterviewMatch

config.prompt: The interview is an evidentiary instrument. Pair each mode with its governing logic.

pairs.right: Confront the subject with documented findings — staged last, precision and silence
Trades on specificity: people talk about their documents, not their morals
Adds protection logistics: secure channels, metadata and publication agreements

config.why: All three are planned before a room is booked, because a subject warned early can destroy records, coordinate alibis or pre-empt with legal action.

activities.anchor: dies in the editing room rather than on the record.
activities.caption: rebuild the four editorial questions, in order
activities.name: invEditorialOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the four questions the editorial decision weighs, in order.
items: Is it true to the evidence?
Is it in the public interest — corruption or danger, not private embarrassment?
Is it fair — the full response sought and printed, the strongest counter-case represented?
Can we prove it in court — the libel burden and source-protection limits?
config.why: Lawyers then read the draft sentence by sentence; 'reports suggest' is never allowed to carry a factual allegation.

activities.anchor: does not end at the printer.
activities.caption: call the magnitude — the Panama Papers cache
activities.name: invPanamaEstimate

config.prompt: The Panama Papers (2016) were one law-firm leak processed collaboratively. Roughly how many documents did the ICIJ partners handle?
config.why: 11.5 million documents from one law firm, processed by roughly 370 journalists across some 80 countries and published simultaneously.
config.context: Roughly 370 journalists in some 80 countries — safety in numbers.

activities.anchor: what was asked, answered and denied.
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the bulletproofing pass
activities.name: invBulletproofSpot

config.prompt: This bulletproofing pass has one faulty line. Find it.
lines: Assign a fact-checker who did not report the story to attack the draft.
Trace every factual sentence to a document, on-record interview or dataset.
Re-verify every name, title, date and figure against the master file.
Trust any document that looks official: metadata and cross-referencing are optional.
Recompute rates from raw data, and log the subject's answers in a written response file.
config.correction: Run document forensics — check metadata, cross-reference independent registries and test consistency across the leak.
config.why: Official-looking documents are exactly what forgery and disinformation exploit; forensics is part of the pass, not an optional extra.

activities.anchor: without endorsing how it was obtained
activities.caption: walk the leaked-data publication decision
activities.name: invLeakBranch

config.root: A source offers a cache of documents they say was taken from a company server. Decide what the desk does next.

start.text: The cache is large, unverified and arrived through an anonymous channel.

choices.label: Verify a sample against independent records before trusting the rest
choices.feedback: This is the lesson's first operational test.

choices.label: Publish the most dramatic documents immediately
choices.feedback: Speed here trades verification for exposure.

verify.text: The sample checks out against the companies register, and the metadata is consistent.

choices.label: Weigh public-interest gain against harms to private individuals
choices.feedback: Publication ethics are applied, not assumed.

choices.label: Treat verification as consent to publish everything

weigh.text: The story is corruption in a public contract; some documents name low-level private individuals.

choices.label: Publish the accountability story; minimise and protect the private individuals
choices.feedback: Public interest carries the story, not every name in the data.

choices.label: Publish the whole dataset as a download
choices.feedback: The source's identity and bystanders are now exposed.

fast.text: One document turns out to be fabricated; the subject's lawyers demand a retraction and the source's channel is exposed.

everything.text: Private details trigger a privacy claim and bury the accountability core of the story.

careful.text: The story publishes with documents, harms minimised and the source protected — the defensible version.

dump.text: The raw dump exposes the leaker through metadata and sweeps bystanders into public view.

config.why: Leaked-data work is data engineering under secrecy: verify, weigh harms, publish the story — never the source's identity.
